newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson to raise profile with Tokyo listing.
newsitem.headline: Henderson to raise profile with Tokyo listing.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to become the first Hong Kong company to obtain a secondary listing in Tokyo with a share offer designed to raise its profile and investor base in Japan.

The Hong Kong property developer said it planned to offer 30 million shares to Japanese investors over the coming weeks. The exact number of shares and issue price has yet to be fixed and the shares would list on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on February 5.
"The board considers that the Japan listing and the Japan offering will provide the company with a more diversified investor base," Henderson Land said in a statement.

"The board considers that the Japan listing and Japan offering will further enhance the reputation and familiarity and promote the recognition of the company among banks, financial institutions and investors in Japan and, thereby, increase recognition internationally," the blue chip company said.

Henderson Land said the proceeds of the offering -- which would total about HK$2 billion (US$258.7 million) based on the HK$72.00 closing price of its shares on Monday -- would be used "for general funding purposes of the business activities of the group".

The shares would represent about 1.73 percent of the company's enlarged issued share capital and would be offered at a discount of not more than three percent to the closing price of its shares in Hong Kong at a date closer to the offering.
Nomura Securities Co Ltd would be the lead manager of the offering.
Henderson Land shares are listed in Hong Kong and also trade in London and, through American Depositary Receipts, in New York.
The stock closed Tuesday morning's session in Hong Kong up HK$0.25 at HK$72.25.
The company said the offering is subject to the finalisation of certain terms and approval from the Minister of Finance in Japan, the Tokyo Stock Exchange and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong.
